chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Jimmy Blanton's influence, 'Jack the Bear', and Blanton, Strayhorn and Ben Webster togethe
summary: Blanton's playing shook up bassists; he and Strayhorn went out with Ben.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did hearing Jimmy Blanton have any affect

Later, yes. When I first met him it didn't have any bearing because as I say I was playing solos too but not the way he was playing them, you know. But when I heard him play 'Jack the Bear,' (laughter) that shook up Basdom. He was a one man rhythm section, you know. That's probably what killed him, over worked. See him playing Guard Dog for Ben Webster and Duke was generally in front of the band, not at the piano. And Sonny Greer wasn't no drummer.
It was in Duke's band that Jimmy Blanton was assigned to take care of Ben?
I've heard descriptions of Jimmy Blanton as a nice quiet, very friendly, nice person. Did he have any trouble? Was it easy for him to take care of Ben? Ben was kind of volatile, wasn't he?

Yes, but he respected Blanton and his musicianship. He says all right Bear, okay Bear, they give him the name Jack the Bear. So later years, there was three of them: Billy Strayhorn, Jimmy Blanton and Ben. They went out together.
Billy watch Ben too? Billy never --
No. Billy was hanging out with Blanton. So he was a tag along, you know, he was real, real passive, you know.
Yeah, he would never argue with anybody.
No, no. He would have a cocktail in his hands, just smiling, be just as gentlemanly (laughter).
